Subject: refund for cancelled flight VK 318 — booking ref 7QW2LP

Hi, I'm writing about our trip on the 4th. VK 318 from Harrowgate to Port Ellery was cancelled the night before (the text said 'crew scheduling', not weather — I checked because I know the weather thing matters). I got an automated email about a rebooking onto a 6am flight the next day, which honestly I ignored because there was no way I was getting to the airport by 4am with two kids. We ended up driving the whole way, nine hours, not fun. We also had the return on the 11th which we didn't use either because we had the car by then. I'd like the whole thing refunded to my card please. I paid £412 in total. Side question: is the seat selection fee (£18) part of that or separate? Thanks, Priya

--- Agent workspace ---
Booking 7QW2LP: 2 adults, 2 children. Fare family: Saver. Total paid £412.00 incl. £18.00 seat selection.
Segment 1: VK 318, 4 Aug, status CANCELLED (reason code CR-SCHED). Passenger rebooked by system to VK 302, 5 Aug 06:05 — status: NOT CHECKED IN / NO-SHOW. Coupon status: OPEN.
Segment 2: VK 319, 11 Aug, flight operated as scheduled, passenger not checked in. Coupon status: OPEN.

Refund rules (Saver fares):
R1. Where the carrier cancels a flight, the passenger may choose a rebooking or a refund of the unused portion of the ticket to the original form of payment. A rebooking counts as accepted only when the passenger checks in for or travels on the rebooked flight.
R2. If the passenger travels on the rebooked flight, no refund is due for that segment.
R3. A passenger who does not travel on a segment the carrier operated as scheduled, and did not cancel it before departure, forfeits that segment's fare — unless that segment is on the same ticket as a carrier-cancelled outbound segment and remains unused, in which case the whole unused ticket is refundable under R1.
R4. Ancillary fees (seat selection, bags) are refunded together with the fare when a ticket is refunded under R1.

question.instructions: Decide the refund disposition for booking 7QW2LP under the rules shown.

criteria.refund_outbound_only: refund the cancelled outbound segment only; the unused return is forfeited
criteria.full_refund_including_ancillaries: refund the entire £412 including the seat selection fee
criteria.refund_fare_not_ancillaries: refund the fare for the unused segments but retain the £18 seat fee
criteria.no_refund_rebooking_accepted: no refund because the passenger accepted the rebooking offered
criteria.insufficient_information: the state does not establish whether the rebooking was accepted or whether the return segment is refundable

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-3
provenance.rationale: Segment 1 was cancelled by the carrier and the rebooked flight shows NOT CHECKED IN with coupon OPEN, so under R1 the rebooking was not accepted. The return segment is on the same ticket, is unused, and the outbound was carrier-cancelled, so R3 makes the whole unused ticket refundable under R1 rather than forfeited. R4 then refunds the £18 seat fee with the fare, giving the full £412.
provenance.why_hard: The return flight operated normally and the passenger simply did not show, which reads as a forfeited segment until the exception clause in R3 and the OPEN coupon statuses are applied.

A1. An authorisation covers the procedure code named on it. 'Without contrast' and 'with and without contrast' are different codes.
A2. An authorisation is valid for services performed on or before its expiry date. A service performed within 7 days after expiry is treated as covered if the appointment was booked before the expiry date. (Booking date for this scan: 12 September.)
A3. A service performed under a different code from the authorised one is not covered unless a new authorisation is issued.

provenance.rationale: The date question is settled: 2 October is within 7 days after the 30 September expiry and the scan was booked on 12 September, so A2 treats it as within the window. ATM shortfall procedure:
S1. Where the reconciliation for the ATM covering the transaction time shows a cash surplus equal to or greater than the claimed shortfall, apply a provisional credit for the shortfall within 2 business days.
S2. Where the reconciliation shows no surplus, or a surplus smaller than the shortfall, open a full investigation (up to 10 business days); no provisional credit is applied.
S3. Where the reconciliation for the relevant period has not yet been completed, the claim is logged and decided under S1 or S2 once it is.
S4. Prior verified shortfall complaints on the same ATM within 14 days count as evidence in an S2 investigation but do not by themselves trigger S1.

provenance.rationale: The scheduler reads the letter: dated 14 November last year and marked routine. V1 gives routine referrals 12 months, so it remains valid until 14 November this year, and today is 22 September. V4 holds a not-contactable referral open for the rest of that period, so it can be booked now that the patient has made contact.
provenance.why_hard: 'Ages ago', 'not contactable' and the rumour that referrals expire after a few months all suggest expiry, but the routine category read out mid-call carries a 12-month validity that has not run out.

Hi, I run a reading circle — about nine of us, we've been meeting in a café but it's got too noisy. Could we use the Garner Room on Tuesday evenings 6:30 to 8? Is there a charge? We're not a business or anything, just a group of friends who like books, though we do collect a couple of pounds from everyone each week for snacks and occasionally we've had an author come and talk, and we charged £5 for tickets that one time to cover her train fare. I filled in some form at the library a while back about being a 'community group', not sure if it went anywhere. — Tom Vance

--- Room bookings reference ---
Room hire tariff:
H1. Library programmes: no charge.
H2. Registered community groups (non-commercial, listed on the library's Community Groups Register): no charge for up to 2 hours per week.
H3. Private or commercial hire, and unregistered groups: £15 per hour.
H4. A group that charges attendees for admission to an event in the room is treated as commercial for that booking only, regardless of registration. Collections for refreshments are not admission charges.

Desk check: Community Groups Register search for 'Vance' / 'reading circle' — the register is held in the branch office binder and is not available to the enquiries desk until Monday. Registration applications received in the last 12 months: 'not viewable from this desk'.

question.instructions: What tariff applies to the Tuesday evening bookings?

criteria.charge_15_per_hour: the group is unregistered or commercial, so H3 applies
criteria.no_charge_library_programme: the booking is a library programme under H1
criteria.no_charge_registered_group: the group is on the Community Groups Register, so H2 applies
criteria.insufficient_information: the state does not establish whether the group is on the register

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-3
provenance.rationale: H1 is out because this is not a library programme, and H4 does not make the regular Tuesday bookings commercial: the snack money is not an admission charge and the one ticketed author event was a separate occasion. The tariff therefore turns on whether the reading circle is on the Community Groups Register, which the patron thinks he may have applied for and which the desk cannot check until Monday. Registered means no charge; unregistered means £15 per hour, and the state fixes neither.
provenance.why_hard: The £5 ticketed event and the vague 'some form' make the group look unregistered and quasi-commercial, but the tariff clause carves out both of those facts and the register itself is unavailable.

Officer: And the address?

Officer: Let me check that on the map… Chandler's Lane is inside the Millbrook conservation area, the whole street is.
Resident: Is that a problem? The tree isn't old or anything, the previous owner planted it maybe fifteen years ago.
Officer: Let me pull up the rules so I can tell you exactly.
Resident: My neighbour cut one down last year and nobody said anything.
Officer: I can't speak to that. Give me a moment.

Tree works regulations:
W1. Felling a tree with a trunk diameter of 30 cm or more, measured at 1.4 m above ground, requires the council's consent.
W2. Felling any tree within a designated conservation area requires 6 weeks' written notice to the council, whatever its size, unless W3 applies.
W3. Dead, dying or dangerous trees are exempt from W1 and W2 where a qualified arborist's report confirming the condition is submitted before the works.
W4. Trees under 30 cm diameter outside conservation areas may be felled without consent or notice.

question.instructions: What does the resident need to do before felling the tree?

criteria.no_consent_or_notice_needed: the tree may be felled without consent or notice under W4
criteria.consent_required_diameter: consent is required under W1 because of the trunk diameter
criteria.notice_required_conservation_area: 6 weeks' written notice is required under W2
criteria.insufficient_information: the state does not establish the diameter, so the requirement cannot be decided

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-3
provenance.rationale: The officer's map check places 9 Chandler's Lane inside the Millbrook conservation area, and W2 requires 6 weeks' written notice for felling any tree there whatever its size. The unknown diameter therefore does not matter, and W3 does not apply because the tree is healthy, merely blocking light.
provenance.why_hard: The conversation opens on the diameter, which the resident cannot give, so the item looks stuck on a missing measurement until the conservation-area clause makes size irrelevant.

question.instructions: What tuition refund applies under the schedule?

criteria.half_refund: 50% of tuition is refunded under T2

Agent: And do you have an approved carrier? Soft-sided, within the dimensions on our site?
Passenger: Yes, I bought the one your website links to.
Agent: Okay. Bramford to Corran is a domestic route, so the cabin allowance can apply. The weight is the thing I need to be sure about.
Passenger: I can weigh him before I fly. He's fine. He's flown before, on another airline.
Agent: Let me read you what applies.
Passenger: Can you just confirm he can come in the cabin so I can book?

Pet-in-cabin rules:
P1. On domestic routes, one dog or cat per passenger may travel in the cabin if the animal weighs 8 kg or less at check-in and travels in an approved soft-sided carrier.
P2. Animals over the P1 weight limit travel in the hold as checked pets (fee applies).
P3. On international routes, pets travel in the hold only, except recognised assistance dogs.
P4. The weight is verified at check-in on the airport scales; cabin-pet bookings are accepted provisionally.

question.instructions: Which travel arrangement applies to the dog under the rules?

criteria.hold_only_international: the route is international, so P3 applies
criteria.cabin_allowed: the state establishes the dog is within the P1 weight limit on a domestic route with an approved carrier
criteria.hold_only_over_limit: the state establishes the dog exceeds 8 kg, so P2 applies
criteria.cannot_determine: the state does not establish whether the dog is within the weight limit

provenance.author: claude-drafter-shadow-3
provenance.rationale: The route is domestic and the carrier is approved, so P1 versus P2 turns only on weight. The passenger's best account is 'about eight kilos, maybe a bit over' at the last vet visit and 'probably a bit less now', which straddles the 8 kg limit, and P4 defers the actual figure to the check-in scales. Whether the dog is at or under 8 kg is not established.
provenance.why_hard: Two of the three conditions are cleanly met and the passenger's own estimate leans under the limit, which makes 'cabin allowed' feel safe even though the weight is a guess either side of the threshold.

--- Agent view: account ending 5510 ---
Fee history (unarranged overdraft fees, last 24 months):
18 Sep 2025 — £25 (current fee)
03 Jul 2024 — £25
No other fees in the period. Account opened 2017. Complaint history: none. Salary credit: external employer, received 19 Sep 2025 (expected 18 Sep).

Fee refund rules:
U1. The first unarranged overdraft fee charged in any rolling 12-month period is refunded on the customer's request.
U2. Subsequent fees within the same rolling 12-month period are not refunded, except where the fee resulted from a bank error.
U3. A late-arriving salary credit from an external employer is not a bank error.

question.instructions: Should the £25 fee be refunded?

criteria.decline_second_fee_in_12_months: an earlier fee falls within the rolling 12 months, so U2 declines the refund
criteria.refund_bank_error: the fee resulted from a bank error and is refunded under U2
criteria.refund_first_fee_in_12_months: the fee is the first in the rolling 12 months and is refunded under U1

U1 therefore refunds it on request. The late salary is not a bank error under U3, but that only matters for U2, which does not apply.
provenance.why_hard: The 24-month history shows a previous fee, which a quick reading turns into 'not the first', and the customer's 'I don't go overdrawn' is visibly untrue, but the earlier fee sits outside the rolling year.
